text:
Letter dated April 14, 1972, re Nebraska Office of Planning and Programming, from Assistant Director, Nebraska Game and Parks Commission.
Comment: Relates to the legislation rather than the draft environmental statement. The writer objects to the removal of non-migratory endangered species from State jurisdiction. He suggests that the States be allowed to retain jurisdiction unless they fail to enact State legislation complementing the Federal law.
Response: It is the spirit of the proposed Act, that endangered species are the property of the people of the United States as part of their national heritage. We feel that placing all endangered species under Federal protection immediately with enactment of the proposed legislation will result in wider dissemination of protection and more universal knowledge of that protection. There is no question that the Department would be dependent upon State enforcement officers for aid in enforcing the Federal protection.
Comment: Nebraska has suggested that suspension of a Federal hunting and fishing permit for violation of the Federal endangered species law would be discriminatory against people with hunting and fishing licenses.
Response: We agree, and the present draft of the bill goes on to provide for suspension of any Federal grazing permit held by one convicted of violation of the Act. But, in the interest of the species involved, we believe this discrimination is warranted. Every individual of an endangered species is particularly valuable and must be protected even if it is by discriminatory provisions.
